title: Inlet water valve fault
shortDescription: Dishwasher is not filling within the expected time.
fullDescription:
Dacor dishwashers display ER1 when the float switch does not detect water reaching the proper level within the fill timeout.

Check the supply shut-off, inlet hose, and the inlet valve solenoid.

fixSteps.title: Open supply
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the supply valve under the sink is fully open.

fixSteps.title: Clean inlet screen
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect inlet hose and rinse the screen.

whenToCallPro: If supply is fine and screen is clean, the valve may need replacement.

faq.q: Could it be a frozen line?
faq.a: Possible if pipe runs through cold space.

title: Drain fault
shortDescription: Dishwasher cannot drain within the expected time.
fullDescription:
ER2 is shown when residual water remains after the drain cycle. Causes include clogged filter, kinked drain hose, or failed drain pump.

Clean the sump filter first - this resolves most ER2 cases.

fixSteps.title: Clean filter
fixSteps.instruction: Twist out sump filter and rinse.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Straighten the drain hose, check the air gap.

whenToCallPro: If pump is suspected and inaccessible.

faq.a: If so, check the knockout plug was removed.

title: Heater circuit fault
shortDescription: Heating element not reaching target temperature.
fullDescription: ER3 means the water did not reach the expected heat-cycle temperature within the timeout. Typically a failed heating element, thermistor, or relay on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Test element
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance of heating element (~25 ohms).

whenToCallPro: If access requires pulling the dishwasher.

faq.a: Yes, helps drying but will not fix ER3.

title: Overfill / leak detection
shortDescription: Float switch or leak sensor activated.
fullDescription: ER4 indicates the leak/overfill safety triggered. The dishwasher will pump out and stop. Inspect the base pan for water and the door gasket for cracks.

fixSteps.title: Inspect base pan
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the kick plate, check for water in the pan.

whenToCallPro: If leak source is not obvious.

faq.a: No - the unit drains and stops automatically.

title: Door latch fault
fullDescription: ER5 means the door switch is not registering the door as closed. Inspect strike, switch wiring, and tank alignment.

fixSteps.title: Adjust strike
fixSteps.instruction: Loosen and re-align the door strike.

whenToCallPro: If switch test confirms failure and access is tight.

faq.a: Door should latch with light pressure - do not force.

title: Wash motor fault
fullDescription: ER6 indicates the wash motor is drawing too much or too little current. Cause is often a stuck impeller, failed start capacitor, or seized motor bearings.

fixSteps.title: Clear debris
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sump and clear any glass or food.

faq.a: Broken glass routinely jams pump impellers.

title: Thermistor open
fullDescription: ER7 means the wash thermistor is open. The unit cannot regulate temperature and aborts the cycle. Replace the thermistor.

faq.a: No - thermistor is required for safety.

title: Thermistor shorted
fullDescription: ER8 reports a shorted thermistor. Same fix as ER7 - replace the sensor.

title: Communication error
shortDescription: UI and control lost serial link.
fullDescription: ER9 indicates loss of communication between the control panel and main board. Reseat the door harness and reset.
whenToCallPro: If reset and inspection do not clear.

faq.a: No - settings are stored on the main board.

title: Main control failure
fullDescription: ER0 indicates the main control failed power-on self-test. Replace the control board.

faq.a: Yes - 30 minute breaker cycle before replacing.
